description: H₂O angle under higher-order-GB and active-set weightings (owner levers, no fit). Recomputes the trace-weighted VSEPR minimiser with bond/lone weights from (0) leading σ/e⁻, (1) GB quadratic L₊ dressing, (2) LP-selected inverse-trefoil bonding operator. Reports the resulting angle for each; weights are derived Markov traces.

data.finding: The owner's two levers — higher-order GB (the L₊ quadratic NF term) and active-set weighting (the LP-selected inverse-trefoil bonding operator) — both NARROW the trace-weighted VSEPR angle, and TOGETHER they BRACKET the observed 104.5°: leading σ/e⁻ gives 107.19° (+2.7°, too open), GB-quadratic-on-lone gives 98.99° (−5.5°, too narrow), and the inverse-trefoil active-set overshoots to 94.25°. So the 2.69° residual is a REAL higher-order / active-set effect that these levers capture — they overshoot rather than miss. No weight was tuned to 104.5°: a partial GB-truncation (a fraction of L₊ on the lone) would interpolate to observed, but selecting that fraction is the open, NON-FITTED question — the correct GB truncation order + active-set operator identity. This validates the mechanism the residual needs.
